Message from the Superintendent

Dear GGUSD parents and guardians,

As we start a new school year, I wanted to follow-up with all parents regarding the video that recently brought an avalanche of media attention to our district and Pacifica High School. The video depicted a group of students engaged in Sieg Heil salutes while singing along to a Nazi marching song. The images captured on the video were shocking and inexcusable. As part of our expanded investigation, the district continues to compile more visual evidence of the incident, which confirms the repulsive actions that occurred.

On behalf of the Board of Education and all staff, I want to be clear in stating that the behaviors seen in the video are in direct violation of our district’s mission, vision and core values. Although the video was taken prior to a school-sponsored event and in a different location, the connection to our school/district and impact on the community has been devastating.

News coverage unfairly and inaccurately implied that such behaviors have been fostered at the school. We know that is NOT the case. Our schools instill values of respect, tolerance, and inclusivity for everyone. We work hard to ensure that our campuses and school district have a climate where such behaviors are prohibited and where students are encouraged to safely speak up immediately to trusted staff members to ensure that bias and hate speech is not tolerated.

When it occurred last spring, our staff handled this incident as a confidential student disciplinary action per our Board policies and student code of conduct. We could not publicly report those disciplinary actions to our community because of strict student privacy laws. We have a responsibility to adhere to privacy laws even when students act so poorly.

In the aftermath of this terrible incident, we have taken additional actions to ensure a safe and welcoming school environment:

District and school administrators are working collaboratively with the Garden Grove Police Department to investigate all allegations of hate speech. All students engaged in hate speech will face disciplinary action in accordance with California Education Code. We hope this will also serve as a learning opportunity for the students involved to show them that there are severe consequences for these types of actions. While discipline is warranted, an equally important goal is to change their behavior and attitudes moving forward.

District officials are working closely with the Anti-Defamation League, the Simon Wiesenthal Museum of Tolerance, The Holocaust Museum, and other similar organizations to identify resources to support students, staff and our community in moving forward to ensure a welcoming and inclusive climate at every school. This will include annual visits to the Museum of Tolerance and collaborating with our partners on a variety of programs.

The District is in the process of forming a Human Relations Task Force as part of our new “Choose Wellness” campaign with a focus on ensuring a safe and welcoming climate on all campuses. We will provide ongoing updates about the work of the task force when it begins.

In February 2017, our Board of Education unanimously adopted Board Resolution 20 to provide reassurance to our families and communities that GGUSD schools are safe and welcoming places for ALL students and families. The Board has already been working on a soon-to-be-adopted Resolution on Goal 2/Wellness and an upcoming Goal 2/Wellness campaign. We will continue to address bias/hate speech issues at district trainings for parents, students and staff, including new Trustee Area forums as a part of our campaign “ChooseWellnessGGUSD.”

We are proud of our highly diverse population and we will continue to do all we can as educators to encourage a culture of understanding, care, and inclusivity. Addressing hate and bias is a community-wide responsibility and we know our parents and community stand behind us. Please join us in our efforts by reporting any incidents of hate speech or bullying to our anonymous hotline, WeTip, at 1-855-862-8559.

We sincerely appreciate your support, patience, and understanding as we work together to foster positive cultures built on respect and kindness. That IS the Garden Grove Way!

Sincerely,

Gabriela Mafi, Ed.D.
